newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat posts firm rise on good grain prospects.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat posts firm rise on good grain prospects.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange wheat futures posted firm gains on Wednesday in reaction to a generally strong market and good local export prospects.
January 1998 posted a single-lot trade, moving up by A$1.00 a tonne to A$170.00 in Wednesday floor trading.
Near-term contract settlement prices rose more sharply, with May and July 1997 both up A$5.00, to A$183.00 and A$184.00 a tonne respectively, and September 1997 up A$7.00 to A$179.50.
This followed strong performances on Australia's overnight SYCOM system where May and July 1997 rose by A$3.00-A$3.50 a tonne in eight lots traded.

Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said Australian wheat futures were up on Australia's excellent export prospects, a good technical and fundamental outlook, the easing Australian dollar and strength in U.S. grains markets.
Rising demand from Asia underpinned Ords' analysis that SFE wheat futures may consolidate around present levels before moving higher, Booth said.
Good inquiries were being received from producers which were beginning to look like hedging at present favourable prices.

Soybean futures' pleasing overnight rise in Chicago, promoted by a rare USDA mathematical miscalculation which earlier overstated quarterly stocks figure, was also based on strong consumption and came despite a big soybean crush, he said.
"Consumption in the grain market in total is surprisingly strong (supporting) the whole grain complex," Booth said.
